editorial:
Imagine being the only person in your family who can hear. That is Ruby's life. She works on her family's fishing boat every morning before school, then rushes to choir practice where she discovers she actually has a real talent for singing. Her parents and brother are deaf, so they do not fully understand her passion. When the family business faces trouble, Ruby feels pulled in two directions. Do you chase your own dream, or stay and help the people who need you most? The movie feels warm, funny, and deeply human from the very first scene.

The acting is wonderful, especially the way the family communicates with sign language and humor. You will laugh at their teasing and maybe tear up during the emotional moments. The music scenes are beautiful and give the story real heart. The only downside is that the plot follows a familiar path, so you might guess where things are heading. Still, it is a feel-good story worth your time. If you love family dramas with heart, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ruby auditions for Berklee College of Music. Her family sits in the balcony, unable to hear her sing. During her performance, her father watches her face and feels the vibrations, finally understanding her gift. Ruby gets accepted and leaves for college. Her family supports her dream, and she promises to stay connected. It is a happy, emotional ending about letting go and believing in yourself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas with heart and music.
